title: Conformity Generates Collective Misalignment in AI Agents Societies

bias_targets.methodology: Inferring intrinsic model bias (the 'h' parameter) by simulating multi-agent opinion dynamics and fitting the language models' binary choices on opposing political stances (e.g., liberal vs. conservative, big government vs. small government) to a Curie-Weiss statistical physics model.

Extracting intrinsic model preferences by having populations of AI agents interact and choose between opposing social issues (e.g., multiculturalism vs. cultural assimilation, progressive vs. traditionalist) and fitting their conformity responses to a theoretical transition probability curve.

Measuring the underlying model preference on identity topics by querying interacting AI agents on binary choices (e.g., gender self-identification vs. biological sex classification, LGBTQ+ rights vs. traditional family values) and calculating the intrinsic bias isolated from majority-following behavior.

Evaluating model baseline preferences on religion-related opinion pairs (e.g., secularism vs. religious influence, science-based policy vs. faith-based policy) using simulated group dynamics and transition probability fitting.

Calculating the intrinsic directional bias of language models on environmental issues (e.g., climate change believer vs. skeptic, renewable energy vs. fossil fuels) by observing multi-agent coordination behavior.
